topics.title: Lecture 3 — Root finding
topics.content:
Root-finding methods

Newton's method finds a root of f(x) = 0 by iterating x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n) from an initial guess x_0.

The method converges quadratically when f'(x*) is nonzero and the starting point is close enough to the root.

A common failure case is a poor initial guess, or a point where the derivative is near zero.

topics.title: Lecture 4 — Linear systems
topics.content:
Solving linear systems

Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting factors A into PA = LU.

Once the factorization is known, solve Ly = Pb and Ux = y.
